title: Monetary policy, strategy and implementation
summary: The ECB publishes a research agenda outlining six broad research areas related to monetary policy: transmission channels, side effects of accommodative policy, forward guidance, implementation issues, the 'new normal' of low natural rates and effective lower bound constraints, and policy normalisation. This page is a section index listing research themes rather than a specific publication, policy decision, or data release. key_points: ECB identifies six general research areas: monetary policy transmission, side effects of accommodative policy, forward guidance, monetary policy implementation, the 'new normal' (ELB constraints), and policy normalisation
Research on transmission focuses on heterogeneity across households, firms, banks; survey data for expectations; bank-level lending conditions; and climate change implications
Side effects research examines costs/benefits of negative deposit rates, asset price/wealth/income inequality effects, and financial stability implications
Forward guidance research covers theoretical effectiveness determinants, empirical evidence, and optimal design
Implementation research addresses money market functioning, Basel III implications, climate change effects, and the collateral framework
Policy normalisation research examines pace and combination of interest rate and balance sheet normalisation, and role of banking/financial conditions
